units.title: Pronouns
units.intro: Grammar: subject, object, possessive and reflexive pronouns, and using it / its for things.

cards.title: Pronouns
rule: A **pronoun** takes the place of a noun so that we do not repeat it: *Aster is late. **She** missed the bus.*

**Subject pronouns** (*I, you, he, she, it, we, they*) come **before the verb**: ***She** writes.* **Object pronouns** (*me, you, him, her, it, us, them*) come **after a verb or a preposition**: *The teacher helped **her**. This letter is for **me**.*

**Possessive adjectives** (*my, your, his, her, its, our, their*) go **before a noun**: *the dog wagged **its** tail.* **Possessive pronouns** (*mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs*) stand **alone**: *The book is **mine**.* They never take an apostrophe: *its, hers, theirs* (*it's* = it is).
**Reflexive pronouns** (*myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves*) point back to the subject: *They did the work **themselves**.* (✗ *theirselves*, ✗ *hisself*)
Use **it / its** for things and animals, **he / she** for people: *The school opened **its** new library.*

**Two names joined by "and":** cover the other name and test the pronoun alone: *The teacher asked Ruth and (I / me)…* → *asked **me*** → *asked Ruth and **me***. *(I / Me) and Aster went…* → ***I** went* → *Aster and **I** went*.

examples.text: Aster and I went to the market.
The teacher gave the books to Ruth and me.
Me and Aster went to the market.
examples.fix: Aster and I went to the market.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: My sister and ____ are going to Asmara next week.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** The pronoun is part of the subject (before *are going*).

**Step 2:** Cover *My sister and*: *__ am going* → **I**.

**Step 3:** *me* is an object pronoun; *myself* needs *I* as the subject.

**Tip:** Before the verb → subject pronoun (I, he, she, we, they). After a verb or a preposition → object pronoun (me, him, her, us, them). Cover the other name and test.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.why:
**Step 1:** *company* is a thing (singular) → *it*.

**Step 2:** Before a noun (*name*) we need the possessive adjective **its**.

**Step 3:** *it's* means *it is* – "has changed it is name" makes no sense.

**Tip:** If you can say *it is*, write *it's*; otherwise write *its*.

cards.title: Choose subject or object pronouns
cards.problem: Correct the sentence: "Between you and I, Abel and me were the only ones who finished."

steps.text: **Step 1: After a preposition use the object form.** "between" is a preposition → between you and **me**.
**Step 2: As the subject of a verb use the subject form.** "Abel and me were" → Abel and **I** were.
**Step 3: Test by removing the other person.** "me were" is wrong; "I was/were" form is right; "between I" is wrong.
**Tip:** cover "you and" or "Abel and" and say the sentence with the pronoun alone.

cards.answer: Between you and me, Abel and I were the only ones who finished.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The scholarship committee awarded the funding to Aster and ________ after reviewing our academic portfolios.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Look at the sentence**
The pronoun follows the preposition 'to' and forms part of a compound prepositional object ('to Aster and [pronoun]'). This slot requires the objective case (Preposition + Object Pronoun).

**Step 2: Watch out for the trap**
Students often write 'Aster and I' because 'Aster and I' is common in the subject position. This is a common pronoun trap in exams. Applying the Cover-Up Test ('awarded the funding to me') makes the correct choice clear.

**Step 3: In Tigrinya**
እቲ ተውላጠ ስም ድሕሪ 'to' ዝብል መስተዋድድ (preposition) ስለ ዝመጸ፡ ኣብቲ ተቐባሊ ሓሳብ (objective case) ክስራዕ ኣለዎ። 'I' (ዋና ባእታ) ኣብዚ ቦታ ክኣቱ ኣይኽእልን እዩ። ነቲ 'Aster and' ዝብል ሓረግ ብምኽዋል 'awarded the funding to me' ኢልና ክነንብቦ ከለና ቅኑዕ መልሲ 'me' (Option B) ምዃኑ ንርዳእ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The old typewriter in the headmaster's office is still functional, but ________ keys are difficult to press.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Look at the sentence**
The blank modifies the noun 'keys' to show ownership. This requires the possessive adjective 'its'.

**Step 2: Watch out for the trap**
Students often confuse 'its' (possessive adjective) with 'it's' (contraction of 'it is' or 'it has'). Option C ('its'') is a non-existent spelling. This spelling distinction is highly tested in national exams.

**Step 3: In Tigrinya**
ኣብዚ ቦታ ናይ ወንነት መግለጺ ቅጽል (possessive adjective) እዩ ዘድልየና። 'Its' (ናቱ/ናታ ንዘይህይወታውያን) ዝብል ቃል ብዘይ ኮማ (apostrophe) ይጸሓፍ። 'It's' ግን ሕጽር ዝበለ ናይ 'it is' ስለ ዝኾነ ኣብዚ ቦታ ኣይሰርሕን እዩ። ቅኑዕ መልሲ 'its' (Option B) እዩ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The teacher asked Ruth and ____ to collect the books.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** "Ruth and ___" is the object of "asked".

**Step 2:** Object position needs an object pronoun: me.

**Step 3:** Test: "The teacher asked me".

**Tip:** Use subject pronouns (I, he, she, we, they, who) before a verb and object pronouns (me, him, her, us, them, whom) after verbs and prepositions. Test a compound by removing the other person.

a pronoun that shows who owns something and stands alone: mine, yours, hers, theirs.
a pronoun that points back to the subject: myself, themselves.
